extracted.intended_audience: NSF NRT awardees (PIs and trainees), institutional administrators, evaluators, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on NSF NRT monitoring system
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting public comments and complying with the National Science Foundation's Research Traineeship (NRT) Monitoring System information-collection requirements, including understanding required data categories, reporting frequency, burden estimates, and the purposes for which NSF will use the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment invitation topics (PRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are invited on: (a) whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information shall have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the Agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information on respondents, including through the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology; and (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency explicitly requests comment on each of the four PRA-prescribed topics (a)-(d). Respondents should address these specific points to assist NSF in its OMB clearance submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting frequency and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: NRT awardees will be required to report data on an annual basis for the life of their award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monitoring system replaces periodic research performance progress reports and requires annual submissions for each award throughout its award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data categories to be collected
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection generally includes three categories of descriptive data: (1) Staff and project participants; (2) project implementation characteristics; and (3) project outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category is collected to serve specific evaluation purposes: staff and participant data are necessary to determine individual-level treatment and control groups for future third-party study or for internal evaluation; project implementation characteristics are necessary to identify well-matched comparison groups; and project outputs are necessary to measure baseline for pre- and post- NSF-funding-level impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored question subsets by participant type
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRT monitoring system includes subsets of questions aimed at different project participants (i.e., Principal Investigators (PIs), and trainees) and allows for data analysis and data report generation by authorized NSF staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system is a web-based data collection tool that provides tailored instruments for distinct respondent roles to capture role-specific information and enable authorized staff reporting and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of a census (vs. sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since this collection will primarily be used for accountability and evaluation purposes, a census, rather than sampling design, typically is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF expects full coverage of awardees/projects for evaluation and accountability; commenters may address feasibility and alternatives but the stated preference is for a census approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimate (hours and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated at 82 hours per award for 120 awards for a total of 9,840 hours (per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF requests comment on the accuracy of this burden estimate (topic (b) of the PRA comment invitation). Respondents should provide supporting data or rationale if they believe the estimate is too high/low or can be reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of collected information
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF will primarily use the data from this collection for program planning, management, performance and audit purposes to respond to queries from the Congress, the public, NSF's external merit reviewers who serve as advisors, the NSF's Office of the Inspector General, and as a basis for either internal or third-party evaluations of individual programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The collection is intended to support accountability (President's Accountability in Government Initiative; GPRA), strategic-plan measurement, and may be used by internal or external researchers/evaluators to identify control/comparison groups and conduct rigorous studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data utility for research and evaluation (control/comparison identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the individual project level some descriptive data are necessary to determine individual-level treatment and control groups for future third-party study or for internal evaluation and to identify well-matched comparison groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data elements must be sufficient to support rigorous research designs and portfolio-level evaluation; commenters can advise on what specific data elements best enable identification of comparison/treatment groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data as baseline for impact measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Project outputs are collected and necessary to measure baseline for pre- and post- NSF-funding-level impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output measures should be designed to permit before/after comparisons; commenters may recommend specific output metrics or methods to improve baseline quality and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for funding adjustments based on survey responses
rubrics_metrics.description: At the individual project level, funding can be adjusted based on individual project responses to some of the surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should be aware that reporting content could affect funding; commenters may address fairness, due process, or recommended safeguards if funding decisions are informed by collected data.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB clearance term and administrative identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF will prepare the submission requesting Office of Management and Budget (OMB) clearance of this collection for no longer than 3 years. OMB Number: 3145-0263. Expiration Date of Approval: December 31, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the requested maximum clearance period and provides the administrative OMB number and expiration; commenters may reference these when submitting PRA-related comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural submission requirements and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments on this notice must be received by March 31, 2026 to be assured consideration. Comments received after that date will be considered to the extent practicable. Send comments to address below. For further information contact Suzanne H. Plimpton, Reports Clearance Officer, with provided phone and email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should submit comments by the stated deadline and may use the provided contact details (including TDD/FIRS) for accessibility; timely submission is necessary for assured consideration in the OMB review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility contact provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who use a telecommunications device for the deaf (TDD) may call the Federal Information Relay Service (FIRS) at 1-800-877-8339, which is accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year (including Federal holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF provides an accessibility channel for contacting the Reports Clearance Officer; commenters requiring accommodation are directed to this service.
